About
Based in Seattle, Washington, Carbon Robotics develops artificial intelligence-driven robotics and autonomous tractor kits designed specifically for the commercial agriculture sector. The company primarily manufactures and sells the LaserWeeder, a specialized agricultural implement that utilizes computer vision and thermal laser technology to identify and eliminate weeds without requiring the application of traditional chemical herbicides. By converting standard farming machines into self-driving systems, these hardware solutions address ongoing weed control and labor challenges for commercial crop growers across the industry. To support its hardware manufacturing and market expansion efforts, the enterprise has raised $70 million in total venture funding to date. The corporate leadership team includes Vice President of Advanced Technology John Mey, Chief Engineering Officer Nick Kirsch, and Vice President of Business Development Sam Robertson. Carbon Robotics was founded in 2018 by Paul Mikesell.

Deep Dive
Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based ag‑tech company that builds AI‑powered robotic implements — best known for the LaserWeeder — which use computer vision and high‑power lasers to remove weeds without herbicides or tillage, targeting specialty and row crops to cut weed‑control costs and improve yields. Carbon has expanded its product line (LaserWeeder G2 and modular variants) and autonomy offerings (Carbon ATK) to serve farms of varying sizes and to scale manufacturing from its U.S. facility.
High‑level overview
 Mission (investment‑firm style): Carbon’s stated mission is to design AI‑powered robotics that enhance productivity, improve safety, and elevate quality of life for people in agriculture by providing precision, chemical‑free weed control and operational autonomy.- Investment philosophy (translated to company priorities): Carbon prioritizes deep systems engineering, data‑driven AI models, and product iterations that deliver measurable farm economics (reduced labor/chemicals, faster payback) while scaling manufacturing and service capabilities.- Key sectors: Precision agriculture, farm robotics, autonomous vehicle retrofit solutions for agriculture, and sustainable/organic row and specialty crop production.- Impact on the startup ecosystem: Carbon has accelerated commercialization of advanced robotics + AI in farming, demonstrated a path from robotics R&D to fielded hardware and recurring software/ops services, and helped validate venture capital interest in capital‑intensive ag‑robotics (notable fundraises and Series B in 2021 supported manufacturing scale).
For a portfolio company (concise customer/product framing)
 Product: Carbon builds the LaserWeeder (now G2 product line) — an AI/computer‑vision system coupled with arrays of diode/CO2 lasers, cameras, and lighting to detect and thermally disable weeds at millimeter accuracy — plus Carbon ATK autonomy kits and cloud ops/apps (Carbon Ops Center, Carbon Companion).- Who it serves: Commercial growers across specialty crops and expanding into row crops in the U.S., Canada, Europe, Australia and organic operations, as well as farms seeking autonomy retrofits for tractors.- Problem solved: Replaces or reduces chemical herbicides, labor‑intensive hand weeding, and soil‑disturbing cultivation by precisely eliminating weeds early, lowering weed control costs (company cites up to ~80% reduction) and protecting soil health.- Growth momentum: Product iterations (G2) and modular sizing, a dedicated manufacturing facility in eastern Washington, global field deployments, and continued fundraising and product launches indicate commercial scaling since initial product introductions in 2021 and broader roll‑out through 2022–2025.
Origin story
 Founding and background: Carbon Robotics was founded in 2018 and is led by CEO and founder Paul Mikesell; the team blends robotics, optics, AI, and agricultural engineering expertise.- How the idea emerged: The company pursued a practical, mechanical solution to the global weed problem by combining high‑resolution imaging, deep‑learning plant models, and targeted laser energy to remove weeds without chemicals — a concept proven in prototype testing and lab/field camera labeling workflows.- Early traction/pivotal moments: Key moments include launching the first commercial Autonomous LaserWeeder in 2021, raising a $27M Series B to scale manufacturing in 2021, revealing expanded LaserWeeder models in 2022, and introducing the G2 product line and a state‑of‑the‑art manufacturing facility to broaden market fit and capacity.
Core differentiators
 Product differentiators: Sub‑millimeter targeting at the weed meristem, integrated high‑power laser arrays and proprietary high‑intensity lighting that enable day/night operation, and a growing labeled dataset (tens of millions of plant images) powering Carbon AI accuracy.- Developer / operations experience: Unified software ecosystem (iPad operator app, Carbon Ops Center, Carbon Companion mobile app) and 24/7 remote software support and service plans facilitate deployment and operator monitoring.- Speed, pricing, ease of use: G2 line emphasizes lighter, modular designs, multiple sizes (8–40 ft), increased speed/coverage (e.g., models capable of ~2 acres per hour for some widths), and quoted machine payback within 1–3 years for many operations.- Manufacturing & scale: In‑house manufacturing in eastern Washington and iterative product engineering reduce production friction and support global deployment.- Ecosystem / IP: Patented optics/lighting approaches and large labeled datasets for crop/weed models give Carbon defensible ML and systems advantages.
Role in the broader tech landscape
 Trend leveraged: Convergence of robotics, edge AI/computer vision, and electrified/laser actuation to automate labor‑intensive agricultural tasks while meeting sustainability pressures to reduce agrochemical use.- Why timing matters: Labor shortages, rising herbicide costs and regulatory pressures on chemicals, plus sharper ESG and organic market demand make non‑chemical weed control commercially attractive now.- Market forces in their favor: Larger addressable market as designs expand to row crops, growing farmer interest in tech that lowers input costs, and increasing farm adoption of autonomy/telemetry services.- Influence on ecosystem: Demonstrates a commercial pathway for capital‑intensive ag‑robotics (hardware + recurring software/ops), encourages complementary innovations (autonomy kits, sensing, datasets), and raises standards for field‑proven AI in agriculture.
Quick take & future outlook
 Near term: Expect further field scaling of LaserWeeder G2 variants, expanded autonomy integrations (Carbon ATK) to improve coverage and utilization, and growth in service/ops revenues as fleets are deployed and monitored via Carbon Ops Center.- Medium term trends shaping their path: Broader adoption depends on per‑acre economics vs. conventional herbicide/mechanical methods, continued AI model improvement for new crops/geo zones, and farm financing/lease models to lower upfront buy‑in. Regulatory moves limiting certain herbicides or incentivizing regenerative practices would accelerate demand.- How influence may evolve: If Carbon sustains technology reliability, dataset leadership, and manufacturing scale, it can become the platform incumbent for non‑chemical weeding and tractor autonomy, enabling further modular implements and an installed base for recurring software and data services.
Quick take: Carbon Robotics has moved from prototype robotics lab to commercial fleet operator by marrying large labeled plant datasets and robust engineering to get lasers working reliably in the field; its success will hinge on continued cost‑of‑ownership improvements, geographic/model expansion, and service economics that make adoption compelling for a wide range of growers.

Carbon Robotics Overview
About Carbon Robotics
Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based provider of autonomous LaserWeeder robots for organic farming. The company's machines use computer vision and high-powered lasers to eliminate weeds in crops like strawberries and lettuce without herbicides. Founded in 2018, it has deployed over 100 units across North American farms, treating millions of acres. Recognized by Robotics Business Review as one of 2016's top 50 influential robotics firms, Carbon Robotics partners with growers in California and Washington states to boost yields and reduce labor costs.

A $20 million Series D-2 extension round on October 22, 2025, was led by Giant Ventures, supporting new AI machinery development amid existing products used by hundreds of customers. This follows a $70 million Series D on October 21, 2024, led by BOND with participation from NVentures (NVIDIA), Anthos Capital, Fuse Venture Capital, Ignition Partners, Revolution, Sozo Ventures, and Voyager Capital, bringing total funding to around $157-193 million across seven rounds. The technology operates day and night regardless of weather conditions like wind or rain, and has eliminated over 10 billion weeds to date. It serves markets in the US, Canada, Europe, and Australia, competing with players like John Deere's See & Spray, FarmWise, Verdant Robotics, and Laser Weeding Technologies by emphasizing proven ROI through cost savings and yield gains. On October 21, 2024, Carbon Robotics raised $70 million in a Series D funding round led by new investor BOND, with participation from existing backers including NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), Anthos Capital, Fuse Venture Capital, Ignition Partners, Revolution, Sozo Ventures, and Voyager Capital. This brings the company's total funding to $157 million since inception. BOND's Mood Rowghani will join the board, highlighting the firm's confidence in Carbon Robotics' execution and potential to transform agriculture amid declining agtech VC investment (down 60% since 2021). The proceeds will expand LaserWeeder sales and services into new international markets such as eastern and southern Europe and the Asia-Pacific region, scale manufacturing with a new 24,000 square-foot facility in eastern Washington to meet demand, and fund development of new software and hardware products. CEO Paul Mikesell described the raise as a pivotal milestone to accelerate AI and robotics innovation for sustainable farming. The company has earned recognitions including CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators, and Fortune’s Change the World lists. |

Prior rounds include a $27 million Series B in 2021 and another $27 million Series B extension in 2023. The company had secured over $20 million in bookings by mid-2023 and sold out its 2021 and 2022 models. |

This brought the company's total funding to $67 million at that time. The proceeds were earmarked for expanding sales in North America, scaling manufacturing, developing new software and hardware, and entering international markets. The company's flagship product, the LaserWeeder, is a certified organic solution that uses AI, computer vision, and high-powered CO2 lasers to identify and eliminate weeds with millimeter accuracy, reducing reliance on herbicides, tilling, and hand weeding. It targets conventional, organic, and no-till farming practices, helping farmers cut weed control costs without damaging crops or soil. By the time of the announcement, LaserWeeders had eliminated over 500 million weeds across 40 crops, with deployments planned across 17 U.S. states and three Canadian provinces. Paul Mikesell, CEO and founder, emphasized the LaserWeeder's role in addressing expensive and unreliable traditional weeding methods while preserving soil health. Rob Freelen of Sozo Ventures praised the team's innovation pace. As part of the round, Freelen and Erik Benson from Voyager Capital joined the board. |
| Sep 2021 | Series B | Anthos Capital, FUSE +4Anthos Capital (lead); FUSE; Liquid 2 Ventures; Voyager Capital; Ignition Partners; Bolt | $27M  Carbon Robotics is an agriculture robotics company based in…Carbon Robotics is an agriculture robotics company based in Seattle that develops AI-powered autonomous weeders, such as the LaserWeeder, which uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eradicate weeds without herbicides or soil disturbance, addressing challenges like superweeds, labor shortages, and sustainable farming. The company's flagship Autonomous Weeder improves crop yields, reduces chemical use, and enhances cost predictability for farmers interested in organic and regenerative methods. On September 1, 2021, Carbon Robotics closed a $27 million Series B financing round led by Anthos Capital, with participation from Ignition Partners, Fuse Venture Capital, Voyager Capital, Bolt, and Liquid2 Ventures. This round brought the company's total funding to $36 million and was intended to scale production, expand the engineering team, establish U.S. sales and support, and invest in new products and technology. Anthos Capital highlighted the team's expertise in AI, machine learning, computer vision, and thermal energy as key to driving agricultural innovation. Voyager Capital's Erik Benson noted Carbon Robotics' potential to transform weeding practices and become a major player like Deere & Company. CEO Paul Mikesell emphasized the investment's validation of their mission to solve farmers' toughest problems amid rising herbicide-resistant weeds. The funding enabled operations scaling to meet demand and continued innovation in agtech. Subsequent rounds included a Series C raising $30 million led by Sozo Ventures in 2023, bringing total funding to $67 million, focused on North American expansion, manufacturing, and international markets. A $70 million Series D in October 2024 led by BOND, with NVentures and others, raised total funding to $157 million for global sales growth and new products. |

The company targets sustainable farming by enabling regenerative and organic practices. The company has deployed units eliminating over 10 billion weeds since 2022 and operates a new manufacturing plant in Richland, Washington. Traction includes customers across the U.S., Europe, and Australia, with a software platform offering field analytics for an annual fee. Its product portfolio includes land drilling rigs, electric fracturing equipment, core parts and components of drilling and completion equipment, offshore engineering equipment manufacturing, drilling engineering services, digital products for drilling and completion, as well as new energy equipment and comprehensive services for oil and gas fields, providing customers with a full products and services for energy development. Its segments include land drilling rigs, parts and components, and others; drilling engineering services; fracturing services; and offshore engineering. The land drilling rigs segment derives the majority of the revenue.

Firefly
Firefly AB is a supplier of spark detection, fire and dust explosion protection systems in Sweden. The company develops, manufactures and sells high-tech systems, which detect and minimise the risk of fires and dust explosions. It has two business areas: Industrial applications and Infra systems. Industrial applications include customized fire prevention systems, which monitor industrial processes in areas such as tissue, food, woodworking, bioenergy, and recycling. The business area of Infra systems includes early fire detection in subway-, train-, road or cable tunnel systems by means of multiple-gas detection.

Systems Engineering
Systems Engineering Consultants Co Ltd provides real-time software solutions. It develops real-time software with four business fields: mobile network, internet, social infrastructure system, and space advanced system. Its software offerings include Rtrilo (Ari Trilo), Rtino (Altino), RTMSafety (RTM Safety), airCube (air cube), airLook (EALOK) and airSmartG (Air Smart G).

Aurotek
Aurotek Corp is engaged in the manufacturing, processing, and trading of various automatic equipment and system parts, the manufacturing, processing, and trading of various electronic product process equipment and industrial controllers, as well as automatic smoke exhaust system engineering, building structure vibration isolation system engineering, and distribution, quotation, and procurement of related products from domestic and foreign manufacturers. Its segments are the Automation components operating unit; Automation equipment operating unit; Energy-saving and safety operating unit; and Others. Geographically, it operates in Taiwan, Mainland China, Japan and Others, where maximum revenue is derived from Taiwan.

carbon-robotics-raises-$70-million-funding
Carbon Robotics, a leader in AI-powered farming, announced that it has raised $70 million in Series D financing. The financing was led by new investor BOND with participation from existing investors NVentures (NVIDIA’s venture capital arm), Anthos Capital, Fuse Venture Capital, Ignition Partners, Revolution, Sozo Ventures, and Voyager Capital. This round brings total company funding to $157 million. As part of the financing, Mood Rowghani, general partner at BOND, will join Carbon Robotics’ Board of Directors.
This new funding round will help scale Carbon Robotics’ LaserWeeder™ business, introduce new software and hardware products, and expand state-of-the-art manufacturing capabilities in Eastern Washington. It will also support the company’s growth in new markets and continue its geographic expansion into Eastern and Southern Europe, as well as the Asia-Pacific region.
“Carbon Robotics is uniquely positioned to deploy AI to transform the massive agriculture industry at a critical time,” said Mood Rowghani, general partner at BOND. “Its proven ability to execute and scale, combined with a visionary leadership team, makes it a clear standout in the space. This investment reflects our strong conviction in the central role Carbon Robotics will play in shaping the future of farming.”
Carbon Robotics has quickly emerged as the innovation leader in the agricultural industry with its AI-powered LaserWeeder. Growers in North America, Europe, and Australia have eliminated more than 10 billion weeds across 100 crop types without the use of chemical herbicides, hand labor, or soil disruption.
“This funding represents a pivotal milestone not just for our company but for farmers and consumers worldwide,” said Paul Mikesell, CEO and founder of Carbon Robotics. “We’re leading a transformative shift, and this investment accelerates our ability to pioneer AI and robotics that will reshape farming for generations to come. I’m excited to have the strong backing of BOND and existing investors like NVentures and to welcome Mood Rowghani to our Board.”
The funding comes on the heels of Carbon Robotics’ recognition on the CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company’s Best Workplaces For Innovators, and the Fortune Change The World lists. These accolades underscore the Carbon Robotics team’s passion for innovation that creates a more prosperous and sustainable future.

Carbon Robotics Raises $27M for Its Autonomous Laser-Wielding Robot
The funding will be used to scale the company’s engineering team, establish regional sales teams and innovate new tech.
Written by Gordon Gottsegen
Published on Sep. 01, 2021

Carbon Robotics’ Autonomous Weeder robot in a field. 
Carbon Robotics’ Autonomous Weeder robot in a field. | Photo: Carbon Robotics
On Wednesday, Seattle-based Carbon Robotics announced the closing of its $27 million Series B funding round. Anthos Capital, Ignition Partners, Fuse Venture Capital, Voyager Capital, Bolt and Liquid2 Ventures all participated in the round, which brings Carbon Robotics’ total funding to $36 million to date.
Carbon Robotics builds agricultural robots using cutting-edge technology. Its flagship product is the Autonomous Weeder, which is a tractor-like robot that uses artificial intelligence to spot weeds in a field, and then uses thermal laser technology to kill those weeds.
These 6 Companies Raised August’s Largest Tech Funding RoundsAlso in Seattle
Weeds are a big problem for farmers, taking nutrients away from the crops that farmers rely on for their livelihood. In the past, farmers had to remove these weeds manually or use herbicides, but both of these solutions have their issues. Removing weeds manually requires a lot of labor, while herbicides can take a toll on the environment. On top of that, the frequent use of herbicides results in herbicide-resistant weeds, which makes the use of herbicide less effective.
Carbon Robotics’ Autonomous Weeder doesn’t use chemicals, and it doesn’t use tills that could disrupt the soil. As a result, farmers have lined up to purchase the robot. Carbon Robotics has already sold out of its 2021 and 2022 Autonomous Weeder models, and secured over $20 million in bookings. The company is currently accepting orders for its 2023 model.
The company plans to use this new funding to scale product production, develop new technology, establish regional sales teams and grow its engineering team. The company is currently hiring with over a dozen open roles in sales and engineering.
“This investment further validates our mission to create tools that utilize technology to address farmers’ toughest problems,” Carbon Robotics CEO and founder Paul Mikesell said in a statement. “Weeding is one of the biggest challenges farmers face, especially with the rise of herbicide-resistant weeds and increasing interest in organic and regenerative methods. This round of investment will enable us to scale our operations to meet the increasing demand for this technology. Additionally, this funding will allow our team to continue to innovate new products and identify revolutionary ways to apply technology to agriculture.”
